I was wrong earlier: the answer is **C**. Former testimony under FRE 804(b)(1) requires that the party against whom it is offered had a similar motive to develop the testimony, and the company's motive in the wrongful-termination suit (defending the firing) was not similar to its motive in the products-liability case (disputing structural defects), and he was no longer an employee, so no vicarious-admission or other exception applies. Option D gets the rule wrong, because the company did have the opportunity to cross-examine and the problem is motive, not opportunity.

CONFIDENCE: 70
